> A decade after the codification of the classic Global Business Services (GBS) operational model, the rapid integration of artificial intelligence and semiconductor manufacturing demands a new architectural paradigm. By viewing contemporary supply chain shifts through a socio-technical lens, we examine whether a "Safe and Sustainable by Design" (SSbD) framework can transform modern GBS networks into the ultimate control towers for Industry 5.0.

::: {.callout-note}

## The Conceptual Core: From Cost to SSbD

Can Global Business Services (GBS) units transcend their historical origins as transactional cost-cutting repositories to become the primary orchestrators of a Safe and Sustainable by Design (SSbD) infrastructure for high-tech sectors such as semiconductor and AI? As multinational corporations (MNCs) face intense pressure to reconcile advanced computational capabilities with aggressive carbon-neutral targets, a structural realignment is occurring at the intersection of micro-level niche innovations and macro-level socio-technical landscape regimes.
:::

## 1. Grounding the Paradigm: From KPMG 2016 to ID-306

Ten years ago, the baseline for corporate maturity was anchored in the fundamental principles of the **KPMG 2016 Global Business Services Maturity Model** [@kpmg_2016-GBS]. That seminal framework mapped out an operational trajectory stretching from decentralized, highly fragmented practices (Level 1) to an integrated, outcome-oriented strategic engine (Level 5) [@kpmg_2016-GBS]. In that traditional paradigm, maturity was measured by an organization's capacity to streamline operational dimensions such as *service portfolios, talent management, enabling technologies, process excellence, and enterprise service governance*.

However, as synthesized in our recent working paper [@Liao-2026-ICE-GBS], the classical focus on internal efficiency and standard process normalization is no longer sufficient to cope with contemporary multi-level landscape disruptions, such as the European Union's dual green and digital mandate, the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD), and Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanisms (CBAM).

It updates the foundational KPMG rationale by recasting the modern GBS unit as an **"operational airlock"**. Rather than functioning merely as a shared service platform, the GBS architecture acts as a vital socio-technical mediator that insulates internal corporate operations from external geopolitical, regulatory, and technological volatility. When retrofitted with a **Safe-and-Sustainable-by-Design (SSbD)** framework, the 10 operational dimensions originally identified by KPMG [@kpmg_2016-GBS] evolve into a system-of-systems mechanism capable of managing both the environmental footprint of AI-native agentic workflows and the hyper-complex lifecycles of the semiconductor value chain.

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│             MACRO-LANDSCAPE PRESSURES                  │
│   (EU Dual Mandate, CBAM, Geopolitical Bifurcation)    │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            GBS AS AN OPERATIONAL AIRLOCK               │
│  Translates RegTech, FinTech & SSbD into Workflows     │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│             MESO-REGIME CONSOLIDATION                  │
│       Top-Tier "Middle Power" Regional Hubs            │
│     (Poland AI-Native, Portugal Green Tech,            │
│       Malaysia GBS 5.0 & Semiconductor Gateway)        │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

```

## 2. Empirical Validation across "Middle Power" Hubs

The transition from academic theory to empirical confirmation plays out across three critical geographic "Middle Power" hubs: Poland, Portugal, and Malaysia. Each country's local ecosystem offers unique validation—and occasional rejections—of traditional maturity constraints.

### 🇵🇱 Poland: The Engine Room for Algorithmic Normalization

The Polish ecosystem, long celebrated as a primary shared-services hub in Central Europe, provides empirical proof that process normalization is a strict prerequisite for AI deployment. In line with industry synthesis, executing advanced automation without rigorous process hygiene serves merely as a "multiplier of inefficiency" rather than a true catalyst for value [@itselectaAIGBS20262026].

Data from the Association of Business Service Leaders (**ABSL**) confirms that Poland's modern business services sector has scaled to over 2,000 centers employing upwards of 488,700 professionals, shifting decisively toward fintech and sophisticated AI-native workflows . This massive human infrastructure validates the **Talent-Innovation Thread** of our framework: true digital transformation cannot rely on technology alone; it requires specialized, high-value local talent to navigate complex socio-technical transitions [@abslBusinessServicesSector2025].

### 🇵🇹 Portugal: The Green Tech and Regulatory Airlock

Portugal serves as a vital laboratory for verifying the integration of environmental stewardship with digital infrastructure. Driven by the *Agência para o Investimento e Comércio Externo de Portugal* (AICEP), the national strategy has focused on attracting tech-heavy, sustainable Centers of Excellence (CoE). Reports by **Ivan Oz** indicate that the Portuguese GBS landscape encompasses approximately 270 centers employing over 93,000 professionals [@ozBusinessServiceCentres2025].

Crucially, observations from **ABSL Portugal** reveal that 84% of these centers are actively upskilling their workforces to fulfill demanding Artificial Intelligence and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) criteria [@abslportugalHowAIAutomation2026]. This high concentration of green-certified competencies confirms the **Policy-Compliance Thread** of ID-306, proving that advanced GBS units can actively buffer MNCs against landscape regulatory penalties by running eco-accountable data and analytical registries [@Liao-2026-ICE-GBS].

### 🇲🇾 Malaysia: The Twin Transition and Semiconductor Gateway

Representing the ASEAN-Pacific research nexus, Malaysia offers the ultimate structural confirmation of the Industry 5.0 GBS paradigm. Orchestrated by the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (**MDEC**), the **"GBS 5.0" framework** intentionally targets a human-centric, AI-driven, and impact-focused operational standard [@pikomGBSMalaysiaStrategy2025]. Operating over 750 centers with a talent pool exceeding 250,000 workers, Malaysia has systematically bypassed basic labor-arbitrage traps [@Liao-2026-ICE-GBS].

This is vividly apparent in Penang, where developments like **GBS@Technoplex** are explicitly designed to capture global AI growth and anchor high-value digital innovation [@investpenangPenangUnveilsDevelopment2025]. Because Penang acts as a critical physical node in the global semiconductor packaging, assembly, and testing supply chain, its digital-first GBS infrastructure [@Liao-2026-ICE-GBS] serves as a concrete manifestation of our proposed [**Safe-and-Sustainable-by-Design (SSbD) Chips Value Chain Services (SCVCS)**](https://scvcs.footprints.cv/) model. It demonstrates how orchestration and industrial data spaces can actively monitor material lifecycles and circular efficiencies.

## 3. Synthesis: Insights

A clear set of insights and modifications emerges:

* **Likely Rejection of Linear Progression:** The classical notion that an organization must progress sequentially from Level 1 to Level 5 is likely outdated. Emerging ecosystems demonstrate that hubs can "leapfrog" intermediate structural stages by deploying native AI talents and cloud architectures, trustworthy autonomous AI agents, and immediate green mandates from day one.
* **The Maturity Trap Reframed:** Achieving the highest levels of maturity is no longer an optional luxury or an unnecessary bureaucratic expense. Under the pressures of global decoupling and a bifurcated geopolitical cloud, reaching an integrated, automated, and legally compliant "operational airlock" state is a strategic necessity to protect a firm's license to operate.
* **Human-Agentic Co-dependence:** The empirical records of Poland, Portugal, and Malaysia collectively refute the idea that automated algorithmic workflows will render human capital obsolete [@abslBusinessServicesSector2025; @abslportugalHowAIAutomation2026; @pikomGBSMalaysiaStrategy2025]. Instead, trust-based hybrid work models, data-driven talent pipelines, and continuous workforce reskilling constitute the indispensable foundation upon which sustainable AI platforms must operate.

Ultimately, configuring GBS for SSbD transitions the entire discipline away from backward-looking administrative logging into a forward-looking, planet-centric technology management strategy. By coupling global talent pipelines with industrial data spaces, orchestrated GBS hubs present a viable socio-technical mechanism to mitigate asymmetric vulnerabilities across global production networks, establishing a resilient "third way" for the future of global value chains.
